    <h1>Research</h1>
    <p class="page-intro">I study how genetic and cellular differences shape disease and treatment responses. My work combines reproducible analysis pipelines, statistical modeling, and biologically informed machine learning. I also develop exact algorithms for inference on phylogenetic trees.</p>

  <section id="als" class="project" aria-labelledby="als-title">
    <div class="project-label"><span class="eyebrow">01 · Rare-variant genomics</span><p>Sep. 2026–present<br>MBZUAI</p></div>
    <div class="project-body">
      <h2 id="als-title">Genetic variation and RNA splicing in ALS</h2>
      <p class="project-meta">PhD Researcher · Supervisor: Alla Mikheenko</p>
      <p>I investigate rare genetic variants near TDP-43 binding regions and their potential role in abnormal RNA splicing in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).</p>
      <h3>My contribution</h3>
      <ul class="contributions">
        <li>Built an HPC analysis pipeline to quality-control and harmonize <strong>3,400+ whole-genome sequencing files</strong>, construct a variant catalog, and annotate candidate variants.</li>
        <li>Performed rare-variant burden analyses with local controls and robustness checks for project, ancestry, and influential variants or genes.</li>
        <li>Developed a pilot RNA-seq framework to examine splice-junction and read-level evidence for prioritized variants.</li>
      </ul>
      <p class="methods"><strong>Methods:</strong> WGS/VCF processing, gnomAD, VEP, SpliceAI, rare-variant analysis, Firth regression.</p>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section id="malaria" class="project" aria-labelledby="malaria-title">
    <div class="project-label"><span class="eyebrow">02 · Single-cell immunology</span><p>Aug. 2026–present<br>MBZUAI</p></div>
    <div class="project-body">
      <h2 id="malaria-title">Population differences in immune responses to malaria</h2>
      <p class="project-meta">PhD Researcher · Supervisor: Eduardo Beltrame</p>
      <p>I analyze blood immune cells from Fulani and Mossi children in Burkina Faso to understand how population background and <em>Plasmodium falciparum</em> infection relate to gene expression.</p>
      <h3>My contribution</h3>
      <ul class="contributions">
        <li>Reanalyzed single-cell RNA-seq data from <strong>126 children and 88,784 cells</strong> after quality control.</li>
        <li>Built a reproducible cell-type annotation pipeline using scVI and donor-balanced hierarchical classification with scHPL.</li>
        <li>Compared gene expression at the donor and cell-type level using pseudobulk analysis, with sensitivity and permutation checks to evaluate robustness.</li>
      </ul>
      <p class="methods"><strong>Methods:</strong> Scanpy, scVI, scHPL, pseudobulk analysis, PyDESeq2, Memento.</p>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section id="hyperadrs" class="project" aria-labelledby="hyperadrs-title">
    <div class="project-label"><span class="eyebrow">03 · Computational pharmacogenomics</span><p>Jul. 2025–present<br>Remote collaboration</p></div>
    <div class="project-body">
      <h2 id="hyperadrs-title">HyperADRs: learning relationships between drugs, genes, and adverse reactions</h2>
      <p class="project-meta">Research Collaborator · Supervisor: Jun Wen</p>
      <p>HyperADRs uses hypergraphs to model drug–gene–adverse reaction relationships, connecting predictive models with biological evidence.</p>
      <h3>My contribution</h3>
      <ul class="contributions">
        <li>Designed a biologically informed adverse reaction categorization scheme to reduce label sparsity and improve prediction and ranking.</li>
        <li>Developed query-conditioned hypergraph models and benchmarked them against neural network and graph baselines on held-out entities.</li>
        <li>Integrated gene, pathway, and protein interaction evidence; co-led experimental design, evaluation, reproducibility, figures, and manuscript preparation.</li>
      </ul>
      <p class="methods"><strong>Methods:</strong> PyTorch, hypergraph learning, PharmGKB, DrugBank.</p>
      <p class="project-result"><span class="badge">Co-first-author preprint</span> <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.00137">Read HyperADRs on arXiv <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></p>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section id="pdd" class="project" aria-labelledby="pdd-title">
    <div class="project-label"><span class="eyebrow">04 · Computational phylogenetics</span><p>2026<br>MBZUAI</p></div>
    <div class="project-body">
      <h2 id="pdd-title">Exact phylogenetic distance deconvolution (PDD)</h2>
      <p class="project-meta">Unpublished manuscript for RECOMB 2027 · <em>Report the tolerance, not the count: exact phylogenetic distance deconvolution with incomplete references</em></p>
      <p>I study how many evolutionary sources are needed to explain a mixed sample’s distances to observed leaves of a reference phylogeny, and how missing references affect source counts and the uniqueness of source placements.</p>
      <h3>My contribution</h3>
      <ul class="contributions">
        <li>Developed exact rational solvers for minimum source count, with parameterized complexity analysis of models with a free or prescribed mean pendant length.</li>
        <li>Formulated the minimum fitting tolerance at each source count using rational linear programming, with a linear-time single-source calculation; evaluated reference loss on exact-model and real estimated distances.</li>
        <li>Released a frozen instance bank, archived experimental results, claim-to-record mappings, checksums, and runnable reproduction checks, with bulk per-run records in the versioned release.</li>
      </ul>
      <p class="methods"><strong>Methods:</strong> Phylogenetics, exact algorithms, parameterized complexity, rational linear programming, scientific reproducibility.</p>
      <p class="project-result"><span class="badge">Code and data released</span> <a href="https://github.com/Haotian-Tang/recomb2027-pdd">GitHub repository <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a> <a href="https://github.com/Haotian-Tang/recomb2027-pdd/releases/tag/v1.0.0">v1.0.0 release <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></p>
    </div>
  </section>
